stem: Sam is a 16-month-old infant with a first episode of wheeze responsive to salbutamol. He has been admitted overnight and is now requiring salbutamol 4-hourly and is ready for discharge. What device is most appropriate for Sam?

options.text: Metered dose inhaler (MDI) and small volume spacer with face mask
Metered dose inhaler (MDI) and small volume spacer with mouthpiece
Metered dose inhaler (MDI) and large volume spacer

explanation: For a 16-month-old child, salbutamol is best delivered by MDI with a small-volume spacer and face mask. A mouthpiece is usually not feasible at this age, and dry powder devices require sufficient inspiratory effort. Nebulizers are generally not preferred for stable discharge therapy when a spacer can be used effectively.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part A

rationale: This is a device-selection question based on age. Infants and toddlers typically use an MDI with a spacer and face mask.

optionExplanations.A: Nebulisers are not the preferred device for routine discharge treatment when a spacer can be used.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: suitable for an infant/toddler who cannot use a mouthpiece.
optionExplanations.C: A mouthpiece is usually not suitable for a 16-month-old child.
optionExplanations.D: Large-volume spacer is not the standard age-appropriate device here; the key issue is the face mask attachment for this age.
optionExplanations.E: Dry powder devices require a stronger inspiratory effort and cooperation, so they are not appropriate for a 16-month-old.
